Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Latin word

accidō

accidō, accidere, accidī

verb, third conjugation; impersonal accidit, with the dative of the person and ut with the subjunctive

happen, occur; befall

In this lexicon

  • happen

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Fam. 14.8.1: sī quid acciderit novī; Caes. BG 4.29.1: accidit ut esset lūna plēna

Notes

  1. 1accidī: short i in the perfect (Lewis & Short ac-cĭdo, cīdi, the perfect of ac-cīdo, cut down). A compound of cadō, cecidī; Lewis & Short marks the perfect short in the other compounds: dē-cĭdo, cĭdi; incĭdo, cĭdi; occĭdo, cĭdi.

Examples

  • Item posthāc, sī quid opus erit, sī quid acciderit novī, faciēs ut sciam.

    And in future too, if anything is needed, if anything new happens, let me know.Cic. Fam. 14.8.1

    In the entry for happen

  • Eādem nocte accidit ut esset lūna plēna

    That same night it happened that there was a full moonCaes. BG 4.29.1

    In the entry for happen

  • sed heus tū! quid agis? ecquid fit?

    but hey, you! How are you? Anything happening?Cic. Fam. 7.11.2
